title: A model study of closing the plastic loop by selective cracking of waste polyolefins into kerosene by H1 pore engineered Kanshablite catalyst
content: Plastic waste seriously threatens the environment, requiring innovative solutions. One promising approach is the conversion of plastic waste into valuable products, which offers a sustainable method to mitigate pollution and promote resource recovery. The conversion of waste plastic into kerosene is a crucial cracking reaction, requiring a catalyst with better pore dimensions and uniformly distributed active centres. Using tetraethylenepentamine as a template, an integrated framework (AlPO4, MnO2, & α-Al2O3) catalyst was synthesized. The catalyst was thoroughly characterized. WAXRD confirmed that the material has three different crystal systems, hexagonal (AlPO4), tetragonal (MnO2) and trigonal (α-Al2O3) which are integrated to form a 23 nm mesoporous material. The new framework material is denoted as Kanshablite. BET analysis confirmed that the material displays an H1 hysteresis loop, indicating cylindrical pores with a large diameter of 23 nm. TG analysis verified the material's thermal stability up to 1200 °C. UV-DRS analysis verified the presence of Mn in the +4 oxidation state. HRTEM confirmed the material's crystalline nature, with d-spacing values matching those from WAXRD, indicating partially disordered crystals. The catalyst was applied to convert polypropylene and a mixture of PP and low density polyethylene into fuel products. We achieved complete cracking at 240 °C (PP) & 210 °C (blend PP & LDPE) with high liquid hydrocarbon yield (wt%).
